title: National park

definition.text: A government-owned and protected area of natural, semi-natural or developed land set aside for conservation because of its outstanding national natural, historic or cultural value.

facts.text: Yellowstone, established by the United States in 1872, is widely held to be the world's first national park.
The IUCN classes national parks as Category II protected areas; in 1971 its criteria included a minimum size of 1,000 hectares and a ban on exploiting natural resources.
Many countries use the term loosely; in the UK a national park is a scenic, lightly developed area with planning limits and may contain sizeable settlements.
Parks Canada, set up in 1911, is the world's oldest national park service, and Canada has 450,000 km2 of national park space.
Parks support nature-based tourism; in Costa Rica park tourism rose by 400% from 1985 to 1999.
Critics say parks in former colonies removed native communities and reinforce the idea that nature is protected only where people are absent.

contested_note: Critics see national parks in former colonies as a form of eco-land grabbing that displaced native communities.

title: Public participation

definition.text: Involving the public, especially those affected by or interested in a decision, in the activities and decisions of an organisation or project.

facts.text: Its core principle is that people affected by a decision have a right to take part in making it.
It is more inclusive than stakeholder engagement and implies that public input can change outcomes.
It is recognised as an environmental principle and enshrined in the Rio Declaration.
Because government alone cannot solve environmental problems, involving the public can improve transparency, accountability and compliance with environmental law.
Low-income citizens often struggle to take part because of childcare costs, time off work and limited access to education on public matters.
The hoped-for gains in public trust from participation have yet to be confirmed.

related: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
